manifest.intent: Test the unchanged reviewed semantic crawler SDF program against a second homogeneous family whose dominant gestalt is vertically concentrated anterior mass over a compact multi-contact footprint.

donors.visualSelectionRationale: Tallest admitted member: a vertically extended macrocephalic anterior lobe, narrow frontal projection, and compact four-point stance make it the strongest height-to-footprint challenge in the family.
Broad cranial bridge over a compact central trunk and four laterally planted contacts; it supplies the widest head-to-body ratio and strongest left-right asymmetry among the upright members.

Large perforated cranial shell over a narrow vertical torso and compact low feet; it tests whether the family fit can express broad elevated mass without turning the organism into a horizontal crawler.

A bulbous upright mass carried by a low radial arrangement of contact appendages; retained as the family-edge member because it shares vertical mass concentration while replacing the cranial bridge with stacked spherical lobes.

visualInspection.visibleDelta: All four fitted donors improve coarse occupancy and depth over the crawler default, but the unchanged crawler program fails the family gestalt in the exact-camera witnesses. Basin 03 preserves frontal height while collapsing its tall anterior mass into a low crawler from side and diagonal views; Basin 10 flattens the broad cranial bridge and compact central trunk; Basin 22 replaces the elevated perforated shell with a rounded crawler body; LIRM 02 loses the stacked bulbous mass and low radial contact arrangement. The evidence supports a second upright-macrocephalic topology program, not cross-family transfer of the crawler program.
